focus: Improve accuracy, cost, and measurement trust using the actual sampling, hashing, and Jev call paths.
noveltyJustification: This pass adds implementation-level findings absent from iteration 1: row hashes are not checked when windows are rebuilt, construction labels are assumed, call payload and local-log boundaries differ, and both call and git-read costs have concrete optimization paths.
keyQuestions: Which label, sampling, hash-validation, reporting, or holdout changes would make the measurement more trustworthy?
What accuracy and call-cost improvements are supported by the current scorer, and what tradeoffs would need a new paired evaluation?
How many calls and what latency were observed, and what content crosses the backend boundary?
answeredQuestions: Use stratified live holdouts, independent annotation/adjudication, construction-label audits, row-hash checks, interval reporting, and explicit skipped status.
The Jev arm plans one auth plus three calls per eligible row and may retry exit 4; a staged rerun/cache needs paired holdout validation.
For K=40 the run planned and recorded 121 calls; sentence, target path, and window are sent to Jev. Dollar cost is unknown without billing data.
ruledOut: Treating automatically shifted windows as proven contradictions without an audit.
Replacing three reruns with fewer calls without an independent paired validation.
Assuming local call logs hold the prompt payload based only on the packet's note; the inspected logger fields do not include it.
nextFocus: Inspect semantic checks elsewhere in .skilled and assess default-on integration needs, risks, and per-run cost.

title: Stored claim/window hashes are not checked when rows are scored
finding: Drawn labels include short claim and window hashes, but buildWindows reconstructs the stored commit locations without comparing those hashes. Add a stale/tamper check before scoring.
inference: Checking both hashes would detect labels/locators that no longer match their intended source text; a deliberate tampering fixture would confirm the guard catches it.

title: Separate and audit constructed rows from live gold labels
finding: The 40-row sample is 20 operator-labeled live citations and 20 automatically construction-labeled windows moved 60 lines within the same file. Keep constructed stress rows separate and audit that each truly contradicts its claim.
inference: An unrelated shifted window may still support the claim by coincidence; human audit and live-only holdout metrics would measure this risk.

title: Add independent holdout and uncertainty by sample stratum
finding: The fixed 40-row, single-commit report provides point estimates and a paired sign-test result; separate live/constructed results, increase live coverage, use a held-out commit or skill, and report confidence intervals for key error rates and paired gain.
inference: This should clarify external validity and sampling uncertainty; the resulting intervals on a representative independent sample would confirm whether apparent gains persist.

title: Current Jev arm plans 3K+1 calls before retries
finding: The scorer makes one auth test and three noul calls per ready labeled row, with one retry on exit code 4; K=40 therefore plans 121 calls, matching the recorded run. Test staged repeats and content-addressed caching only against an independent holdout.
inference: Fewer calls may lower backend spend and latency but may worsen modal-label stability; a controlled holdout comparison would quantify the tradeoff.

title: Semantic requests transmit document content to Jev
finding: The Jev arm passes a JSON payload with the citing sentence, target path, and cited window to the backend. The inspected local logger stores call metadata only; this should be reconciled with the packet note that calls.jsonl holds doc text before any default-on rollout.
inference: Actual provider retention and any separate CLI-level logging are not established by the caller; provider/runtime retention documentation and the historical calls artifact would confirm them.

title: Memoize committed file reads after profiling
finding: The default scan is recorded at about 171 seconds and committed-file reads spawn git show; window reconstruction can reread target paths. Cache committed text by commit and path, then compare end-to-end runtime and identical output.
inference: Repeated target reads make memoization a plausible improvement, but profiling the default scan would confirm how much time it saves.

title: Distinguish skipped, partial, and completed semantic runs
finding: The current CLI may exit zero when the Jev arm is skipped or stopped. Scheduled integration should surface explicit semantic status, reason, and measured denominator rather than leave a successful process code to imply completed evaluation.
inference: An explicit status field should reduce operator confusion; an integration-level acceptance criterion can verify that skip reasons are visible.
